title: Gradient Accumulation and Resetting
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of gradient accumulation and resetting in a PyTorch workflow.

content.intro: Gradient Accumulation and Resetting: Autograd records differentiable tensor operations in a computational graph and applies the chain rule to calculate derivatives during backward propagation. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: Gradients show how a loss changes as parameters change; they are the signal used by optimizers to improve a model. For this lesson, focus on why gradients accumulate and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Set requires_grad only for values to differentiate, compute a scalar loss, call backward(), inspect .grad, and reset gradients before the next optimization step. The source topics for this lesson are: Why gradients accumulate, zero_grad(), Gradient accumulation across batches. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import torch
x = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
(x * 3).backward()
(x * 4).backward()
print(x.grad.item())

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Gradients accumulate by default; reset them at the intended point and avoid unsafe in-place mutation of values needed by autograd.

common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
